clue.text: Maybe fellow Arab business leader in position on board

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: stalemate is a chess position where the side to move has no legal move

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of business is taken

explanation.surface: An Arab businessman holds a seat on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is a horse breed, not a person: a horse sharing a stable with another is its stablemate. 'on board' means a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses trained in the same stable are companions there, so one Arab horse may be another's companion.

clue.text: Small squads' joint means of transport?

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
squads are teams
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A shared ownership arrangement among small squads, a question of how they travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam carries passengers and goods, an example of transport, hence the question mark.

clue.text: He criminally assists one higher up the social scale

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
people of higher social rank were once called their betters

explanation.surface: A man from a superior class helps out in a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice who helps or encourages wrongdoing is said to aid and abet, giving this agent noun.

clue.text: Like text of Times leader initiated in Lincoln?

parts.note: times are eras

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Abe was US President Abraham Lincoln's familiar name

indicators.note: initiated means just the start of the word leader is used

explanation.surface: Asks what the leading article of The Times was like when started in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' looks like a newspaper editorial, but the two words split: Times is one piece, and 'leader initiated' means only the first letter of leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in pencil or on a whiteboard can be rubbed out, so text is often removable that way.

clue.text: What may be father's doing that Irish boy breaks law

indicators.note: breaks means one piece cuts into the other, opening it up

parts.note: a father is a parent, so something he does may be called an act of a parent
Liam is a common Irish boy's name

explanation.surface: Dad's work is the reason an Irish lad gets into trouble with the law.
explanation.walkthrough: LIAM breaks into the phrase ACT OF PARENT after its PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by the UK legislature is a law, so the phrase is a formal name for legislation.

clue.text: German socialist's son following in French set

indicators.note: following puts the son's letter after the rest

parts.note: en is French for in
to gel is to set, as a jelly does
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A German socialist's boy is part of a French group.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels, Marx's collaborator, was a German political theorist of the communist movement.

clue.text: Swallow nervously, after commercial setback

indicators.note: setback read as set back means the word is turned round

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, a commercial mention

explanation.surface: Someone gulps in alarm after a business setback.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a quick anxious swallow is the classic sign of nerves.

clue.text: Ensure beneficiary receives universal aid at first

indicators.note: receives says the first piece takes the others inside it

parts.note: a grantee is one who receives a grant, a beneficiary
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: at first picks just the opening letter of aid

explanation.surface: Someone makes sure a beneficiary gets universal help from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain or secure something is to give a promise or pledge that it will happen.

clue.text: Six-footer in study lacking a source of light

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
lacking says the letter is taken out

parts.note: to study is to learn
an insect such as the ant has six legs, so six feet

explanation.surface: A very tall person in a study without any light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; here it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp in a protective case, carried or hung, gives illumination.

clue.text: Trumpeter messing up central part of The Planets

indicators.note: messing up means the letters are jumbled into a new order
central part of drops the outer letters of the two words and keeps the middle

explanation.surface: A trumpet player fluffs the middle section of Holst's The Planets suite.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of THE PLANETS, losing outer T and S, is HEPLANET, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The great beast's call is called trumpeting, so it is a cryptic trumpeter.

clue.text: Poet without quarters, one possibly given a flat?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the poet goes round the rest

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy in a Country Churchyard
the compass points are quarters; N twice gives two of them

explanation.surface: A poet with no lodgings, someone perhaps offered an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without quarters' reads as homeless but means GRAY outside two compass points, here N and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny flat is a self-contained annexe for an elderly relative, so a grandmother may be given one.

clue.text: Dish out a source of protein, say

indicators.note: say shows that the word is spoken, giving one of the same sound

parts.note: meat is a rich source of protein

explanation.surface: Serving up some protein at mealtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or distribute, as punishment or rations are handed out.

clue.text: A chap on a horse reportedly in partnership

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: a chap is a Ted, and a horse is a filly; putting a Ted after a filly gives the sounds 'a filly a Ted'

explanation.surface: A rider is said to be in business with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'a filly, a Ted' resembles the answer; 'on' puts the chap after the horse in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being officially attached or connected to an organisation means being joined with it as an associate.

clue.text: Demanding clue concocted by a woman's aunt, oddly

parts.note: her is a woman's possessive word

indicators.note: concocted means the letters are cooked up into a new order
oddly takes the first and third letters of aunt

explanation.surface: A woman's aunt has made up a strangely tough crossword clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A task needing great strength or effort, like the labours of the hero Hercules, is extremely taxing.

clue.text: Part uncle fluffed, suffering from overindulgence

indicators.note: an actor who fluffs a line garbles it, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An uncle forgets his lines in a play because he is hungover.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone sick from excessive eating or drinking, a hangover state.

clue.text: Smart fleece?

definitions.meaning: to smart is to hurt with a sharp pain
to fleece is to swindle, overcharge someone

explanation.surface: Is a woolly coat stylish?
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pain is felt like a prick, and slang for a swindle or con is the same word.

clue.text: A drop recklessly imbibed by fellow sponsor

indicators.note: imbibed by says the jumble is swallowed inside the next word

parts.note: a gent is a fellow

indicators.note: recklessly says the letters are thrown about in no set order

explanation.surface: A man who sponsors something carelessly downs a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stands as sponsor at a baptism takes on spiritual care of the child.

clue.text: Do this to horse, having most enjoyable trip

parts.note: best means most enjoyable, finest
a ride is a trip or outing

explanation.surface: Someone tells a rider to mount up for the most enjoyable excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit astride a horse with a leg each side is what a rider does when mounted.

clue.text: Contemptuous expression getting second husband in scrape

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to paw the ground is to scrape it, as a horse does

explanation.surface: Getting a second husband lands someone in a fix, to scornful remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: This old exclamation voices disdain or impatience, like 'pooh' or 'bah'.

clue.text: Fork out pounds for investing in plant

indicators.note: for investing in says the next letter is put inside the plant

parts.note: spurge is a plant, a euphorbia
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: Someone pays out money to buy into a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory; it is the weed SPURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money freely and lavishly is to pay out cash, as a slang phrase says.

clue.text: Sad to confront a serial wife-killer

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
to beard someone is to confront them boldly

explanation.surface: It is sad to face up to a murderer of several wives.
explanation.definitionFit: In Perrault's folk tale the nobleman murders a series of brides, so he is the figure of a wife-murderer.

clue.text: Some wag it at owners in frenzied manner

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some dogs wag their tails at their owners in great excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a musical direction meaning to play in an agitated, excited way.

clue.text: Intelligence a prince displayed, moreover

parts.note: wit is intelligence, quickness of mind
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A prince showed his cleverness, and more besides.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning besides or in addition, as well as.

clue.text: It lights up sick deer, for example, right away

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: away says the letter is removed

parts.note: deer chew the cud, so they are cud-chewers

explanation.surface: Something illuminates a sick deer, then the right goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that gives out light, such as a lamp, is a light source in technical language.

clue.text: Capital city this writer's visiting?

indicators.note: visiting says the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, the city
the setter refers to themself as this writer, so this writer is is I'm

explanation.surface: Which capital is the setter in town to see?
explanation.definitionFit: The Peruvian seat of government is a capital city.

clue.text: Report of quarrel bringing part of firearm

indicators.note: Report of says the word is heard spoken

parts.note: a breach is a rift or quarrel

explanation.surface: A gunshot in a dispute damages part of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' suggests a gunshot, fitting the firearm, but it signals the spoken word.
explanation.definitionFit: The back part of a gun barrel, where the cartridge is loaded, has this name.

clue.text: Move abroad in Russian plane with energy and speed

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft maker
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone flies off overseas in a fast Russian jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving one's home country to settle in another is relocating overseas.

clue.text: Church officer, one who spoke Manx, for example

definitions.text: one who spoke Manx, for example

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Lt is a lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: A church official who spoke the Isle of Man's old language.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is a Gaelic tongue, so its speakers belong to the ancient people of Ireland, Scotland, Wales and Man.

clue.text: Antisocial type distributing papers, etc

parts.note: a person who drops rubbish such as paper wrappers scatters it in public places

explanation.surface: An unfriendly person handing out leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carelessly drops rubbish in the street is called this, the British term for such a person.
